meta.description: EdCo combines education intelligence, research, content, events, marketing and technology to help organisations understand what schools and trusts need, engage the right educators and turn those relationships into awareness, leads, pipeline and long-term growth.

hero.heading: Helping organisations build better relationships with education.
hero.standfirst: Understand educators. Create value. Build engagement.
hero.body: EdCo combines education intelligence, research, content, events, marketing and technology to help organisations understand what schools and trusts need, engage the right educators and turn those relationships into awareness, leads, pipeline and long-term growth.

partners.heading: Schools need partners, not vendors.
partners.body1: Schools don’t wake up hoping to hear from another supplier. They have problems to solve, outcomes to improve and very limited time.
partners.body2: If you want a meaningful relationship with educators, start there. Understand what they need. Be useful. Earn attention. Build trust.
partners.close: Then you’ve got a considerably better basis for a commercial conversation.

howItWorks.heading: Listen. Understand. Give. Engage. Build. Grow.
howItWorks.lead: One model, running underneath everything we do. Where you join it depends on what you’re trying to achieve.
howItWorks.closeLead: Then your sales team does the
howItWorks.closeBody: We can create the opportunity. At some point, you still have to sell. EdCo does not offer outsourced sales representation — we make the conversation worth having.

outcomes.heading: Start with your objective. Not our organisation chart.
outcomes.lead: You don’t need to know which EdCo product or team you need. Tell us what you’re trying to achieve. We’ll work out what combination of intelligence, people, technology and engagement capability makes sense.

oneEdco.heading: One EdCo. Lots of ways to help.
oneEdco.lead: We don’t expect you to work out which one you need. That’s our job.

breadth.heading: The problem with starting with a supplier is that you often end up starting with their solution.
breadth.body: Sometimes the answer is research. Sometimes it’s better intelligence. Sometimes it’s a different proposition, useful content, an event, a campaign, technology or several of those things together.
breadth.close: And sometimes the best advice is to change the plan altogether.

proof.heading: Relationships measured in decades, not campaigns.
proof.bodyBefore: Some customers have worked with EdCo for more than
proof.body2: Not because we’ve kept selling them the same thing. Because their objectives have changed, education has changed and we’ve changed with them.

logos.heading: Great organisations. Different objectives. One thing in common.
logos.lead: They want to understand education better and make a greater difference within it.

hearing.heading: What we’re hearing from educators right now
hearing.lead: Not education news. What educators are actually telling us — and what it might mean for organisations working with education.
hearing.cardNote: Each item answers: what are educators telling us, where are we hearing it, why it matters, and what it could mean for organisations working with education.

freeValue.heading: Something useful before we ask you for anything
freeValue.lead: Give to receive works for us too.

featured.title: What don’t you know about your customers?
featured.body: Send us your customer list. We’ll analyse it through Education IQ and an EdCo person will walk you through what’s in there.
